blockers.what: The read path was rewritten to eliminate fflate's unbounded worker fan-out, but the write path still calls fflate's asynchronous `zip`, which has exactly the same fan-out. `zip` loops over every entry with no queue and no concurrency limit and calls `term.push(deflate(file, p, cbl))` for every member of 160000 bytes or more (node_modules/fflate/lib/index.cjs:2280-2284), each of which spawns its own worker_threads Worker. Peak memory is therefore the sum over members plus one V8 isolate and one structured-clone copy of the input each — the identical quantity r4 blocked on the read side. Measured end-to-end through the shipped API: a 240 KB `.sloodge` (150 x 300 KB members, 43 MB declared inflated) is ADMITTED by `readDeck` under the shipped defaults (ok:true, 150 extras, read peak ~43 MB), and `writeDeck` of that same bundle peaks at 1912 MB RSS (+1687 MB delta) in 7.3 s. Scaling is linear at ~11 MB of RSS per member: 64 -> +719 MB, 128 -> +1309 MB, 256 -> +2878 MB. `DEFAULT_ARCHIVE_LIMITS` admits 10,000 entries and 256 MB total, so a deck this module itself accepts extrapolates to ~11 GB on save — an OOM kill of the Electron main process, the exact failure r4 recorded.
blockers.why: `extras` round-trips verbatim by design (§5.2), so open-then-save of an untrusted deck is the exploit, and the caps that gate `readDeck` do not bound the *write* peak any more than they bounded the old read peak. Worse, the file's own docblock at store.ts:11-13 states that writing 'spawns a `worker_threads` Worker' (singular) and never discloses the fan-out, while lines 15-21 spell out at length that the same fflate behaviour was fatal on read; the plan-doc line added in this diff (.claude/plans/init/11-tech-stack.md:38) likewise attributes the fan-out only to `unzip`. A reader of this changeset is told the hazard was eliminated when half of it was not.
blockers.fix: Swap `zip` for `zipSync` in `zipAsync` (store.ts:668-675), or drive fflate's streaming `Deflate` one member at a time the way `extractMembers` drives `Inflate`. Measured on the identical 150 x 300 KB input: async `zip` = +1748 MB / 7.07 s, `zipSync` = no net RSS growth (GC ran during it) / 0.58 s — the sequential path is both bounded and ~12x faster here, so there is no trade to make. Then correct the docblock at store.ts:11-13 and the tech-stack row so the fan-out is attributed to fflate's async API generally, not to `unzip` alone, and add a test mirroring 'inflates one member at a time' for the pack side.

majors.what: `inflateMember` silently accepts a DEFLATE member that produces fewer bytes than it declared, and the `while (at < source.length)` loop at line 580 never runs at all when `compressedSize === 0` — so the stream is never pushed, `final` is never set, and the member returns 0 bytes with no error. Verified through the real API: taking a normal saved deck and zeroing the slide member's `compressedSize` in both its local and central headers makes `readDeck` return `ok: true` with `bundle.slides[id] === ''` and `warnings === []`, and re-saving that bundle writes a 0-byte `slides/<id>.html`. Every other size disagreement in this file is fatal (a merely truncated stream correctly yields `not-a-zip: unexpected EOF`), so this is the one hole in an otherwise complete contract.
majors.why: Silent data loss on a corrupt or tampered deck: the user opens the file, sees an empty slide with no warning of any kind, saves, and the content is gone. `readDeck`'s own stated policy for a slide file that is genuinely absent is to repair *and warn* (store.ts:886-889, §2.2 invariant 3); a member that is present but delivers nothing gets neither the repair message nor an error. Not a blocker only because it needs a hand-zeroed header rather than any shape a real zipper produces.
majors.fix: Treat under-delivery as malformed, since for DEFLATE `originalSize` is exact: replace line 593 with `if (produced !== allowed) throw new ZipExtractError(...)` and return `out`. That also closes the `compressedSize === 0` case without touching the loop. If tolerating short members is ever wanted, it must at minimum push a `warnings` entry the way the missing-file path does.

majors.what: The local-vs-central cross-check that this round's architecture rests on is not pinned by any test. Deleting the name check (store.ts:542-544) leaves all 160 document tests green; deleting the compression-method check (store.ts:545-547) likewise leaves all 160 green. The racing deadline timer (store.ts:822-830) is also unpinned — replacing it with a promise that never settles still passes 160/160, because the existing 'always settles' test at store.test.ts:1092 is satisfied by the in-loop `Date.now() > deadline` checks alone.
majors.why: These three are the load-bearing new mechanisms of the rewrite — the changeset's own docblock (store.ts:23-31, 64-67) sells them as what replaces the second parser and what guarantees `readDeck` settles. Unpinned, they are one refactor away from silently disappearing, and the next round has no signal that they went. Contrast the rest of the file, which is genuinely well pinned: I reverted eight other guards and six of them turned a test red (ZIP64 count-vs-EOCD divergence, the streaming overflow abort, the `hasZip64` extra-field gate, the STORED `max(originalSize, compressedSize)` sizing, the `totalCompressed > file length` aliasing check, and the pre-allocation entry-count guard that r4 recorded as unpinned and is now covered).
majors.fix: Three small crafted-archive tests: (a) a central entry whose `localHeaderOffset` points at a different member's local header -> expect `not-a-zip` naming the mismatch; (b) a member whose local header declares method 0 while its central header declares 8 -> expect `not-a-zip`; (c) an extraction that hangs in an `await` (e.g. an observer that returns a never-resolving promise, or an injected yield) with `extractionTimeoutMs: 5` -> expect the timer, not the loop check, to settle it.

minors.what: Nit: a blown extraction deadline is surfaced to the caller as `code: 'not-a-zip'`. `DeckReadErrorCode` has no timeout member, so the catch at line 832-834 folds `ZipExtractError('extraction exceeded 30000 ms')` in with genuine parse failures. Confirmed: `readDeck(path, { extractionTimeoutMs: 0 })` on a valid 50-member archive returns `not-a-zip`.
minors.why: The message string carries the truth but `error.code` is what a UI will branch on, so a large-but-honest deck that trips the 30 s ceiling will tell the user their file is not a zip archive — a wrong and unactionable diagnosis to debug from a support ticket.
minors.fix: Add `'timeout'` to `DeckReadErrorCode` and map `ZipExtractError` raised by the deadline to it, the way `ZipTooLargeError` already maps to `'too-large'`.

minors.what: Nit: the copy at lines 841-842 and its comment ('Copy into a null-prototype map: `entries['constructor']` on a plain object would resolve up the prototype chain') have drifted. `extractMembers` now returns `emptyMap<Uint8Array>()` (store.ts:609), so `raw` is already null-prototype and the loop is a no-op re-key of the whole archive.
minors.why: A comment that justifies a defence which the code it guards already provides is exactly the kind of stale rationale that survives into the next refactor and gets cargo-culted. It also touches every entry for nothing.
minors.fix: Drop the loop and use `raw` directly, or keep it and rewrite the comment to say it is a defensive copy against a future `extractMembers` that returns a plain object.

minors.what: Nit: the docblock says peak allocation is `allowed + O(1)`. The real transient is `allowed + ~1 MB`: `MIN_FEED_BYTES` is 1024 (line 521) and a push is only inspected after it returns, so a single push can hand the callback up to 1024 * MAX_DEFLATE_RATIO ~= 1.06 MB (and fflate's `cbuf` doubling can briefly hold ~2x that) before the overflow check at line 571 sees it.
minors.why: The bound is real and small — I confirmed a 40 MB-inflating stream declaring 100 bytes aborts with `too-large` and no measurable RSS growth — but 'O(1)' reads as bytes, not megabytes, and someone sizing `maxEntryBytes` against an Electron memory budget will want the actual constant.
minors.fix: State the constant: 'peak is `allowed` plus at most ~2 MB of transient push output (MIN_FEED_BYTES x MAX_DEFLATE_RATIO, doubled by fflate's internal buffer growth)'.

verification.test: pnpm test — exit 0, 176 passed (7 files); document subset 160 passed
verification.environment: node v24.18.1, pnpm 11.18.0. All adversarial work was done in a scratch copy at $SCRATCH/work with node_modules symlinked; the reviewed tree is byte-identical to the commit (git status unchanged).

hypotheses_tested: H1 (does the r4 memory blocker actually die with the rewrite?): REJECTED as a defect — the fix is real. Re-ran r4's own PoC shape through the shipped `readDeck`: a 190,602-byte archive of 300 x 512 KiB members (150 MB declared inflated) now peaks at 313 MB RSS / +131 MB delta and settles in 2.4 s with `manifest-missing`. r4 measured 3079 MB on the same shape and a host-process kill at 1.17 MB / 950 MB. The +131 MB delta is the retained bundle itself (every inflated member is kept, bounded by `maxTotalBytes`), not fan-out.

H2 (is the fan-out really gone, or did it just move to the write half?): CONFIRMED, and recorded as the blocker. fflate's `zip` fans out identically to `unzip` (index.cjs:2280-2284, worker per entry >= 160000 bytes). Measured through `packDeck`: 64 entries -> +719 MB, 128 -> +1309 MB, 256 -> +2878 MB, all linear at ~11 MB/entry. Measured end-to-end: a 240 KB archive that `readDeck` admits under shipped defaults costs +1687 MB on `writeDeck`. Control: the same 150 x 300 KB input through `zipSync` grew RSS by nothing at all and ran in 0.58 s vs 7.07 s, which both isolates the cause to the async worker path and supplies the fix.

H3 (is any fflate zip *parser* still authoritative in the read path?): REJECTED. The only fflate imports are `Inflate`, `strFromU8`, `strToU8` and `zip` (store.ts:95). `Inflate` is a raw DEFLATE stream decoder with no notion of zip structure, and `strFromU8` is a text decoder; every offset, size, name, method and symlink bit now comes from `scanCentralDirectory`. `unzip`/`unzipSync`/`Unzip` appear nowhere in src/. The two-parser class of bug that produced r2/r3/r4 is structurally closed on read — and correspondingly, the ZIP64 count divergence that was r4's blocker 1 is now merely rejected by the scan (store.test.ts:895 pins it, and reverting the check reds exactly that test).

H4 (streaming abort correctness under a real bomb): REJECTED. Hand-built a single-member archive whose central and local headers both declare `originalSize = 100` over a 40,942-byte DEFLATE stream that inflates to 40 MB. Result: `too-large`, 'archive entry assets/bomb.bin inflates past the 100 bytes it declared', with negative RSS delta (GC ran) — the abort fires long before the 40 MB materializes. Reverting the abort (making the callback drop the chunk instead of setting `overflowed`) reds two tests, so it is properly pinned.

H5 (does the streaming path ever under-deliver silently?): CONFIRMED, recorded as major 1. `compressedSize = 0` on a DEFLATE member makes `while (at < source.length)` never execute, so nothing is pushed, `final` is never set, and the member yields 0 bytes with no error and no warning. Demonstrated on a real fixture deck: the slide opens as `''`, `warnings` is empty, and re-saving persists a 0-byte slide file. The adjacent case (declaring 50,000 more bytes than the stream produces) also passes silently, though there the correct 44 bytes do come through. Ordinary truncation is handled correctly (`not-a-zip: unexpected EOF`).

H6 (local-vs-central cross-check completeness): PARTIALLY CONFIRMED. What is checked — signature, name, compression method, and that the compressed range fits inside the file — is sufficient, because extraction is driven entirely from the central entry the caps were applied to, so the local header's own size fields are never trusted and a data-descriptor (bit 3) member is therefore harmless. What is missing is *tests*: reverting the name check and the method check each leaves 160/160 green. Recorded as major 2.

H7 (deadline / Promise.race edge cases): REJECTED on every axis tried. `extractionTimeoutMs: 0` on a 50-member archive settles in 8 ms; `-100` settles; an empty `wanted` short-circuits to an already-resolved promise and settles. Background work after the race rejects is correctly bounded: with `extractionTimeoutMs: 25` on a 300-member archive, 10 members had started when `readDeck` settled and still exactly 10 after waiting a further 500 ms — the in-loop `Date.now() > deadline` check terminates the orphaned extraction on its next iteration. The timer is `unref`'d and `clearTimeout`'d in a `finally`. The only gap is that the timer itself is unpinned (folded into major 2), and it is arguably inert today since `extractMembers` awaits nothing but `setImmediate`.

H8 (duplicate names / last-wins): REJECTED as a defect. Hand-built an archive with two central entries both named `a.bin` pointing at two different local headers. Both members are started (observer saw ['a.bin','a.bin']), both are charged against `budget` and against `totalCompressed`, and the second overwrites the first in the output map — last-wins, matching fflate's own semantics and the write side's insertion order. No cap bypass: the duplicate is summed twice, which is the safe direction, and `totalCompressed > bytes.length` still catches aliasing (reverting that check reds store.test.ts:781).

H9 (empty and degenerate archives): REJECTED. Zero-entry `zipSync({})` -> `not-a-zip` at the magic-byte gate (a valid-but-empty zip has no local header, so it can never be a `.sloodge` anyway); a 26-byte file that is PK\x03\x04 followed by a bare EOCD -> `manifest-missing`; a directory-marker-only archive -> `manifest-missing`; a file under 22 bytes -> `not-a-zip` via the `eocd < 0` guard. The backward EOCD scan cannot read out of bounds because it starts at `length - 22`, so `eocd + 22 <= length` holds for every candidate it inspects.

H10 (are r2/r3/r4's earlier fixes still revert-proof?): ALL HOLD, and r4's open minors are closed. Reverted ten guards one at a time against the 160-test document suite: ZIP64 count-vs-EOCD divergence -> 1 red; streaming overflow abort -> 2 red; `hasZip64` gate on 0x0001 extra fields (the r3 fix) -> 1 red; STORED `max(originalSize, compressedSize)` sizing (the r3 fix) -> 1 red; `totalCompressed > bytes.length` aliasing check -> 1 red; pre-allocation entry-count guard -> 1 red (r4 recorded this as reddening nothing; store.test.ts:917 now covers it). The ZIP64 locator bounds check reds nothing under a naive revert only because the resulting out-of-range `getBigUint64` throws a RangeError that surfaces as the same `not-a-zip` the test asserts — the behaviour is still pinned. Unpinned: local-header name check, local-header method check, racing deadline timer (major 2).

H11 (repo conventions, trust boundaries, dependency policy): REJECTED. r4's dependency minor is fixed — `fflate` and `zod` are now `catalog:` in package.json with entries in pnpm-workspace.yaml and a justifying row + catalog line in .claude/plans/init/11-tech-stack.md. No native modules. Dependency direction holds: `src/shared/document/**` imports only zod and siblings, `src/main/document/store.ts` imports only node builtins, fflate and `src/shared`; oxlint is green. The single new `oxlint-disable-next-line` (store.ts:658) suppresses `no-await-in-loop`, not a dependency-direction rule, and sequential awaiting is the entire point of that loop. No IPC channel, no `webPreferences`, no iframe sandbox attribute is touched. Both trust boundaries (manifest JSON, theme JSON) are zod-parsed with a `__proto__` pre-scan, never cast. Zip-slip and symlink rejection are unchanged from r4 and still pinned (store.test.ts:364, 1106, 1127). `escapeHtml` covers every interpolation in `createStarterSlideHtml` and the theme-token deny-list from r3 is unchanged.
not_reviewed: pnpm-lock.yaml (generated; the catalog entries it records match pnpm-workspace.yaml and `pnpm lint`/`test` install cleanly).
notes.summary: The read-path rewrite genuinely works: I re-ran r4's own PoC and the 3 GB peak is now 131 MB, the second parser is gone, the streaming abort stops a 40 MB bomb that declared 100 bytes, and six of the previous rounds' fixes are revert-proof with r4's two minors closed. But the same fflate fan-out that forced the rewrite is still live in `packDeck`: `zip` spawns a worker per entry over 160 KB, and a 240 KB deck that `readDeck` itself admits costs +1687 MB on save, scaling linearly to a main-process OOM well inside the shipped caps. `zipSync` on the identical input costs nothing and is 12x faster, so this is a one-line fix, not a trade. Beyond that, a DEFLATE member declaring zero compressed bytes reads as an empty slide with no warning and re-saves as such, and the three new mechanisms the rewrite rests on (local-header name check, method check, racing timer) are each deletable with 160/160 still green.
